Independent majorization and coloring equality-case reconstruction
correctness.rationale: For s zeros, their cross-edge cost is (s²−u²−v²−w²)/2. Sorting occupancies, the first partial sum is at most a and the second at most a+b, as well as at most s. Filling largest shores first attains both partial-sum bounds, so strict convexity of the squares forces the same sorted vector in every equality case. This yields the sharp piecewise lower bound with slopes 0,a,a+b. Its three positive-field vertices are feasible with zero nonpreferred edge cost. At h=0 any proper coloring uses three disjoint nonempty shore color sets and hence exactly one color per shore. At h=a the largest shore must be full of zeros and the extra k may occupy only one other shore. For partial filling of that shore, both nonzero shores are nonempty and must use opposite constant colors; when the shore is exhausted every vertex of the last shore chooses independently. The two cases add, including when their monomials coincide (e.g. k=c on B and all of C). This gives the displayed P_a and its sum 3(2^b+2^c)−6 even for c=1. At h=a+b strict capacities force A and B full; all three colors of each C vertex are free, giving x^(a+b)(2+x)^c. The strict regimes follow from unique minimizing s and the same equality rules. The optional residual-entropy limits follow by bounding the first degeneracy between constants times 2^b and by taking logs of the other exact counts.
residual_risks: The finite author census has only six size triples and eight fields per triple; the conclusion instead relies on the proof. Strict size ordering and the nonnegative-field regime are essential to this classification.

Equality census and comparison with prior field and coloring formulations
value.rationale: An all-size exact finite-field classification for the natural first three-shore family distinguishes independent color choices when a shore is saturated from constrained two-shore choices. It separates two distinct critical entropy mechanisms and also exposes an extensive intermediate degeneracy, neither of which the ground-energy envelope alone determines. The critical polynomials are useful finite-size information, not just checks at chosen parameters.
residual_risks: Crossing fields scale with shore sizes; these are not fixed-intensive-field thermodynamic transitions. No claim for positive temperature or wider multipartite families follows.
